required_repairs.detail: The extra-line cutoff is identity when u=0 only if f0 is the inclusion. An arbitrary isotopy fixed on the base need not have f0=id. State f0=id and tau(s,0)=0 explicitly in the actual comparison and cutoff construction.

The transport paragraph proves preservation when the base homotopy is constant near A, but later tangent-normal identification and equal-normal comparison use prescribed smooth transport on A during a nonconstant homotopy. Supply the stronger relative construction: normalize arbitrary T_t from time0, compare with prescribed S_t by h_t=T_t^-1 S_t, h0=id, extend h_{lambda(b)t} by identity using a cutoff supported in its protected open domain, and replace T_t by T_t h_{lambda t}.

Retain the prescribed smooth normal neighborhood maps/charts, not merely a normal projection or isomorphism of abstract TOP microbundles. Patching away from A must leave these maps unchanged; prescribed smooth vector transport and linear stable isomorphisms there must make the final trivialization representative smooth on the protected germ. Otherwise pulling back the ambient smooth atlas need not agree with the given product smoothing.

support_domain_clarification: Shrink the ambient to the retraction domain, where M is closed by the retraction identity. At each current open-base patch restrict accordingly. Then closed overlap strips and nested support neighborhoods for the cutoff have the stated normal-space separation properties.
independent_checks: The supplied actual tube identifies a compact disk block B0 containing C in its interior. Its abstract smoothing supplies finite charts/collar only; the draft correctly does not equate this with the protected atlas.

The coordinate-package embedding is locally a continuous graph after dividing an active package by its positive partition coordinate, and is a smooth embedding near A. Tietze coordinate transfer of the retained retraction is valid; short-geodesic interpolation can make it the smooth tubular retraction near A without smoothing the remaining base.

The pullback vector bundle has a finite trivial-bundle embedding and continuous projection smooth near A. Relative symmetric approximation and a spectral gap give an actual smooth vector bundle isomorphic to it, with the isomorphism the identity on a smaller protected germ.

For a coordinate base M, H(v,y)=(r(v)+y,v) gives the actual local normal after m stabilization directions. The two tangent normals are related by explicit rotation about the diagonal; the supplied germ transport yields ambient comparison isotopies once its relative form is repaired.

Given f0=id, the extra-line map is an actual conjugate of a level-preserving isotopy. If a moved point exits E0 its new last coordinate exceeds two, preventing collision with the added identity domain below one. This verifies global injectivity near the base rather than inferring it from locality alone.

Finite atlas patching uses a closed transition strip inside the overlap. After comparison cutoff the two projection germs agree there and hence glue. All modifications can remain outside a smaller protected germ, with finite stabilization increments.

The actual normal identities and supplied reduction give tau+nu+epsilon^t = tau+epsilon^(L+q+s). Adding the independently constructed normal eta with tau+eta=epsilon^D gives nu+epsilon^(D+t)=epsilon^(D+L+q+s). No cancellation of a nontrivial microbundle without its actual inverse is used.

With R=D+t and k=D+L+q+s, the product-normal rank equals dim(Y)+q+R-m by m+s=rank(xi)+t. A representative of this trivial normal germ, restricted to continuous positive fiber balls and radially rescaled, supplies an actual homeomorphism M x R^k onto a smooth open neighborhood. The remaining relative smoothness requirement is exactly the map-level repair above.

Countable product-chart witnesses and locally finite countable refinements require at most CC on the second-countable finite-atlas bases; compositions are locally finite. Finite isomorphism manipulations and the proposed protected automorphism cutoff add no arbitrary-index choice.
